transcript.text: my tumble dryer is giving off a burning smell?? is it safe to keep using it

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. A burning smell from a tumble dryer can be overheated fluff from restricted airflow, but it can also be a slipping belt/motor or an electrical fault; all need treating as a potential fire risk and the dryer needs a qualified engineer’s inspection before it is used again. With it unplugged and cool, you can remove and inspect the door fluff filter for heavy lint and check for any obvious scorching or melted plastic without taking panels off. Tell me whether the smell is more like hot fluff/dust, hot rubber, or electrical burning, and whether the filter is badly clogged.
ok I've switched it off at the wall already! the smell is like singed dust or hair?? and the filter is really full, I haven't cleaned it in a few weeks. is that the problem??

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Yes — a filter that full is a very plausible cause. Restricted airflow can make trapped fluff, dust and hair get hot enough to smell singed, but it does not prove that this is the only issue; lint further in the air path or, less commonly, a motor/belt or electrical fault can also smell hot. Clean the door filter thoroughly with the dryer unplugged and cold, and look for obvious scorching or melted plastic. Then check the lower condenser/second filter if it has one, or the rear vent hose if it vents outside, for heavy lint or blockage. Even if you find and clear a blockage, do not use the dryer again until a qualified engineer has inspected it because it has produced a burning smell.
it's a vented one, the hose goes through a hole in the wall. it's squashed behind the dryer and I can see fluff inside the end of it?? is that bad? should I just get an engineer in?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Yes — that is bad, and it is a very likely contributor to the singed dust/hair smell. A squashed hose restricts the air leaving the dryer, and visible fluff in it adds to the restriction, so heat and lint can build up inside the machine. Please get an engineer in and do not use the dryer again until it has been inspected; they should clean the internal air path and check the heater, fan, thermostats and wiring as well as the hose. With it unplugged and fully cool, you can safely pull the dryer forward enough to straighten the hose and remove only loose, reachable fluff from the hose end and outside grille — do not poke tools deep into the duct or open the dryer. The engineer can then confirm there is no scorched lint or heat damage internally.
